Chapter 5: Strengthening Commitment Through Precommitments and Pacts
Even if you’ve learned to spot your internal triggers, built yourself a solid schedule, and cleared away distractions—let’s be honest, temptation still finds a way in. That’s just part of being human. So, what can you do in those moments when your willpower is running low?
Here’s where precommitments come in. Think of these as decisions you make ahead of time, designed to protect your future self from getting sidetracked. It’s like setting up gentle roadblocks before you even reach the intersection of distraction.
Why do precommitments work so well? Because making choices in advance is usually easier than trying to make the right call when temptation is staring you in the face. By setting up clear agreements or rules ahead of time, you make it much simpler to stick to your intentions when you’re feeling tired or distracted.
There are a few different kinds of precommitments—often called “pacts”—that can really help you stay focused:
First up, effort pacts. These are all about making distractions just a little bit harder to access. Imagine you’re about to dive into some deep work. Instead of keeping your phone within arm’s reach, you leave it in another room. Or you log out of your social media accounts so you can’t just click and scroll without thinking. By adding a tiny bit of friction, you give yourself a better chance to stay on track.
Then there are price pacts. This type of precommitment attaches a real cost to giving in to distractions. Maybe you set up a rule: if you check your email during your writing time, you have to donate a few dollars to a cause you don’t support. Suddenly, the stakes are a little higher, and you’re more likely to pause before breaking your focus.
And finally, identity pacts. These are about seeing yourself in a new light. When you start telling yourself—and even others—that you’re someone who values focus, or that you’re “indistractable,” you begin to act in ways that match that identity. It might sound simple, but shifting how you see yourself can have a big impact on your daily choices.
The most effective pacts are the ones you set for yourself—specific, realistic, and not too rigid. The idea isn’t to box yourself in, but to give yourself gentle guardrails that help keep you moving in the right direction.
Let’s look at a couple of real-life examples. Maybe you’re a writer struggling with deadlines. You could use an effort pact by disabling your internet connection during writing sessions. Or, if you and your friends want to stick with a workout routine, you set up a price pact—any missed session means a small penalty goes into a group jar. For someone trying to unplug after work, adopting the identity of a person who values work-life balance, and putting up a visual reminder, can really help.
Precommitments don’t have to be solo efforts, either. Sometimes, sharing your intentions or making a public commitment can boost your accountability. Maybe you tell your coworker you’ll be working without interruptions this afternoon, or you join a group with the same goals—you’re much more likely to stick with it when others are cheering you on.
So, how do you make precommitments work for you? Start by picking pacts that target your biggest distractions. Make your commitments visible—and if it helps, involve someone else for that extra nudge. If things don’t go perfectly? No worries. Review what happened, tweak your approach, and remember, it’s not about being perfect. It’s about learning and moving forward, one step at a time.
Precommitments might not be magic, but they’re a powerful tool for defending your focus. By choosing in advance how you’ll handle temptation, you give yourself the best shot at staying true to your values—even on the days when motivation is nowhere to be found.
And with this step, you’ve got the final piece of the indistractable puzzle: you’ve learned how to manage internal triggers, time-box your actions, cut down on external triggers, and now, how to lock in your commitment with precommitments. Together, these strategies help you take back control of your attention—and live each day with more intention.
